title: OrderedMultiDict equality with plain mappings
issue_text:
`OrderedMultiDict == dict` is True even when the values differ

When I compare an `OrderedMultiDict` with a regular dict, only the keys seem to matter. If the keys line up, `==` says the two are equal even when the values are completely different.

```python
from boltons.dictutils import OrderedMultiDict

omd = OrderedMultiDict([('x', 10), ('y', 20)])
omd == {'x': 10, 'y': 5000}    # True, expected False
```

`QueryParamDict` from `boltons.urlutils` does the same thing:

```python
from boltons.urlutils import QueryParamDict

params = QueryParamDict([('x', '10')])
params == {'x': 'other'}    # True, expected False
```

I expected `==` to be `False` as soon as a value differs, and `True` only when both the keys and the values match.
